intro: Agla Station, a Telegram bot for the Delhi NCR metro, was built in Claude Code over {elapsed_hours} hours, {active_hours} of them active, following a phased plan. The human typed {prompts} prompts and made every product call; Claude took {claude_actions} actions to build, test and check the work. Everything below comes straight from the project's ledger: the hooks recorded each prompt and tool call, and decisions were logged as they were made.

moments.note: Public from the first commit, so the ledger hook had to redact secrets reliably from the start. Later, CI scanned every commit for them too.

moments.match: Manual spot-check caught a fare bug
moments.note: A human spot-check in the DMRC app caught a fare of ₹43 that should have been ₹54, which the 384-fare automated check hadn't flagged.
Both models scored 50/50 on station parsing. Claude suggested checking reply quality before moving to the cheaper Haiku; the human kept Sonnet, whose replies had already been tested on a phone.
The plan's earning rules gave a demo commuter five free day passes a month, so miles were recalibrated before rewards went live.
The planned safety check failed its first live test. Claude fixed the setup; the human cut it down to a traveller-sent "I've reached" instead.
A reviewer subagent that hadn't seen the build audited the code cold. Every finding was fixed or documented, each with a regression test.

moments.match: Metro Wrapped as a three-stop metro ride
moments.note: Wrapped was redesigned twice. The second version was rejected for looking AI-made; the third turned it into a short metro ride built around the bot's name.
The remaining fare misses were fixed using only official data already on hand: all 384 official fares now match.
